result.title: Representation and Model Contributions on Small Molecular Benchmarks: Controlled Comparisons and External Evaluation
result.comment: Accepted at the 2026 7th International Conference on Computing and Informatics (ICCI), Cairo, Egypt. 7 pages plus a 6-page supplement
result.summary: Improvements in molecular property prediction are usually attributed to the model, although part of the gain may come from the molecular representation. New models are commonly benchmarked against a random forest (RF) trained on a molecular fingerprint, a comparison that changes the model and the representation at the same time. We separate the two contributions with a two-by-two factorial design in which the RF and a second model (CatBoost or the tabular foundation models TabPFN and TabFM) are each trained on a fingerprint and on RDKit descriptors, and each effect is tested with a paired scaffold bootstrap. Seven small MoleculeNet datasets (3 regression, 4 classification) are evaluated on the published split of a recent graph transformer (DGT), on 10 additional scaffold splits and on external datasets. For solubility and lipophilicity, the representation effect exceeds the model effect in every main factorial design, in all three evaluations. For hydration free energy, the result depends on the starting fingerprint: from ECFP4 the representation effect is larger, and from MACCS neither effect is significantly larger. On the classification datasets, only one main factorial design has a significant difference between the two effects. Although the model effect is smaller on solubility and lipophilicity, TabFM outperforms the RF on all 7 datasets when both use RDKit descriptors. With RDKit descriptors in place of a fingerprint, the RF baseline reported for DGT surpasses the transformer's published solubility score. We recommend that model comparisons evaluate classical baselines on more than one representation and report the representation and model effects separately.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在七个 MoleculeNet 小分子数据集上用 2×2 因子设计分离「分子表示」（指纹 vs RDKit 描述符）与「模型」（RF、CatBoost、TabPFN/TabFM）对性能的贡献，并以配对 scaffold bootstrap 检验，发现溶解度与脂溶性任务中表示效应更大，建议基线比较分别报告两类效应。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「表示效应 vs 模型效应」的因子分解与配对检验思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 表示与模型结构各自贡献的归因方式；但研究对象是分子性质预测，与视觉多模态推理无直接联系，需较多核查。
